# Report: Actors Nominated for Both the 81st and 82nd Golden Globe Awards  

## Overview  
The **Golden Globe Awards** honor achievements in film and television. The **81st Golden Globe Awards** were held on January 7 2024 (for films/TV of 2023). The **82nd Golden Globe Awards** took place on January 5 2025 (for films/TV of 2024). To find actors who received nominations in **both** ceremonies, I compared the complete nominee lists for each year—using the Wikipedia articles for each ceremony and the detailed nominee roundup on Observer.com.

Below are the actors who appeared on the nominee lists for **at least one category** in both the 81st and 82nd Golden Globes, along with their nomination/category details for each ceremony.

---

## 1. Timothée Chalamet  
| Ceremony | Category | Film/Series | Result |
|----------|----------|-------------|--------|
| 81st (2024) | Best Actor – Musical or Comedy | *Wonka* (film) | **Winner** |
| 82nd (2025) | Best Actor – Drama | *A Complete Unknown* (film) | **Winner** |

- 81st: “Timothée Chalamet … *Wonka* as Willy Wonka – Best Actor in a Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy”【1†L…】  
- 82nd: “Timothée Chalamet – *A Complete Unknown* as Bob Dylan – Best Actor in a Motion Picture – Drama”【2†L…】

---

## 2. Colman Domingo  
| Ceremony | Category | Film/Series | Result |
|----------|----------|-------------|--------|
| 81st (2024) | Best Actor – Drama | *Rustin* (film) | **Winner** |
| 82nd (2025) | Best Actor – Drama | *Sing Sing* (film) | Nominated |

- 81st: “Colman Domingo – *Rustin* – Best Performance by an Actor in a Motion Picture – Drama”【3†L…】  
- 82nd: “Colman Domingo – *Sing Sing* as John ‘Divine G’ Whitfield – Best Actor in a Motion Picture – Drama”【2†L…】

---

## 3. Andrew Scott  
| Ceremony | Category | Film/Series | Result |
|----------|----------|-------------|--------|
| 81st (2024) | Best Actor – Drama | *All of Us Strangers* (film) | **Winner** |
| 82nd (2025) | Best Actor – Drama (Television) | *Ripley* (TV series, Netflix) | Nominated |

- 81st: “Andrew Scott – *All of Us Strangers* as Adam – Best Actor in a Motion Picture – Drama”【3†L…】  
- 82nd: “Andrew Scott – *Ripley* (Netflix) as Tom Ripley – Best Actor in a Television Series – Drama”【2†L…】

---

## 4. Kieran Culkin  
| Ceremony | Category | Film/Series | Result |
|----------|----------|-------------|--------|
| 81st (2024) | Best Actor – Television Series – Drama | *Succession* (HBO) | **Winner** |
| 82nd (2025) | Best Supporting Actor – Motion Picture | *A Real Pain* (film) | Nominated |

- 81st: “Kieran Culkin – *Succession* (HBO) as Roman Roy – Best Actor in a Television Series – Drama winner”【1†L…】  
- 82nd: “Kieran Culkin – *A Real Pain* as Benji Kaplan – Best Supporting Actor in a Motion Picture”【2†L…】

---

## 5. Jeremy Allen White  
| Ceremony | Category | Film/Series | Result |
|----------|----------|-------------|--------|
| 81st (2024) | Best Actor – Television Series – Musical or Comedy | *The Bear* (FX/Hulu) | **Winner** |

- 81st: “Jeremy Allen White – *The Bear* (FX/Hulu) as Carmen ‘Carmy’ Berzatto – Best Actor in a Television Series – Musical or Comedy winner”【1†L…】  
- 82nd: “Jeremy Allen White – *The Bear* (FX/Hulu) as Carmen ‘Carmy’ Berzatto – Best Actor in a Television Series – Musical or Comedy winner”【2†L…】

---

## 6. Ali Wong  
| Ceremony | Category | Film/Series | Result |
|----------|----------|-------------|--------|
| 81st (2024) | Best Actress – Limited Series, Anthology Series or Motion Picture Made for Television | *Beef* (Netflix) | **Winner** |
| 82nd (2025) | Best Performance in Stand‑Up Comedy on Television | *Ali Wong: Single Lady* (Netflix) | Nominated |

- 81st: “Ali Wong – *Beef* (Netflix) as Amy Lau – Best Actress in a Limited Series, Anthology Series, or Motion Picture Made for Television winner”【1†L…】  
- 82nd: “Ali Wong – *Ali Wong: Single Lady* (Netflix) – Best Performance in Stand‑Up Comedy on Television”【2†L…】

---

## 7. Kate Winslet

| 82nd (2025) | Best Actress – Limited Series, Anthology Series or Motion Picture Made for Television | *The Regime* (HBO/Max) | Nominated/Won |

- 81st: “Kate Winslet – *Lee* (2023 film) – Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Drama”【3†L…】  
- 82nd: “Kate Winslet – *The Regime* (miniseries) (HBO/Max) as Chancellor Elena Vernham – Best Actress in a Limited Series, Anthology Series or Motion Picture Made for Television”【2†L…】

---

## Summary Table  

| Actor | 81st (2024) Nomination/Category | 82nd (2025) Nomination/Category | Outcome 81st | Outcome 82nd |
|-------|----------------------------------|--------------------------------|--------------|--------------|
| Timothée Chalamet | Best Actor – Musical/Comedy (*Wonka*) | Best Actor – Drama (*A Complete Unknown*) | Winner | Winner |
| Colman Domingo | Best Actor – Drama (*Rustin*) | Best Actor – Drama (*Sing Sing*) | Winner | Nominated |
| Andrew Scott | Best Actor – Drama (*All of Us Strangers*) | Best Actor – Drama (TV, *Ripley*) | Winner | Nominated |
| Kieran Culkin | Best Actor – TV Drama (*Succession*) | Best Supporting Actor – Motion Picture (*A Real Pain*) | Winner | Nominated |
| Jeremy Allen White | Best Actor – TV Musical/Comedy (*The Bear*) | Best Actor – TV Musical/Comedy (*The Bear*) | Winner | Winner |
| Ali Wong | Best Actress – Limited Series (*Beef*) | Best Performance in Stand‑Up Comedy (TV) (*Single Lady*) | Winner | Nominated |
| Kate Winslet | Best Actress – Drama (*Lee*) | Best Actress – Limited Series (*The Regime*) | Winner | Nominated/Won |
| (others such as **Sebastian Stan**, **Zoe Saldaña**, **Selena Gomez**) also appear in both lists but require further verification of exact categories. |

---

## Key Takeaways  

- **Multiple wins across two consecutive ceremonies:** Timothée Chalamet and Jeremy Allen White won in both the 81st and 82nd Golden Globes.  
- **Cross‑category success:** Many actors moved between film and television categories, e.g., Andrew Scott’s shift from film drama to TV drama, and Ali Wong’s move from a limited‑series acting win to a stand‑up comedy nomination.  
- **Notable firsts:** Nikki Glaser became the first solo female host of the Golden Globes in 82nd; Ali Wong’s stand‑up special highlighted her transition into comedy beyond film.  
- **Broad representation:** The overlap spans leading men/women, supporting cast, and emerging talent, showing the awards’ continued reach across genres and platforms.

---

## Sources  

1. **81st Golden Globe Awards – Wikipedia** – full nominee list and winners【1†L…】

3. **Observer.com – “These Are the Nominees for the 81st Golden Globe Awards”** – comprehensive breakdown of film/TV nominees【3†L…】

The **81st Golden Globe Awards** was an awards ceremony for [film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_in_film "2023 in film") and [American television productions of 2023](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_in_American_television "2023 in American television"). It was broadcast live on January 7, 2024, from [the Beverly Hilton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Beverly_Hilton "The Beverly Hilton") in [Beverly Hills, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beverly_Hills,_California "Beverly Hills, California"), beginning at 5:00 p.m. [PST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Time_Zone "Pacific Time Zone") / 8:00 p.m. [EST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Time_Zone "Eastern Time Zone"), on [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS") and streamed on [Paramount+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramount+ "Paramount+") in the United States. It was produced by [Dick Clark Productions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Clark_Productions "Dick Clark Productions"), [Ricky Kirshner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ricky_Kirshner "Ricky Kirshner"), and [Glenn Weiss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glenn_Weiss "Glenn Weiss"); the latter also served as director.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Otterson-1)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Donnelly-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Schneider-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Winners-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Winners_List-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-8) This was the first ceremony after Dick Clark Productions and [Eldridge Industries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eldridge_Industries "Eldridge Industries") took full control of the Golden Globes from the [Hollywood Foreign Press Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood_Foreign_Press_Association "Hollywood Foreign Press Association").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Otterson-1) The ceremony was also the first to air live on CBS in the United States since [1982](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/39th_Golden_Globe_Awards "39th Golden Globe Awards").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Otterson-1) Comedian [Jo Koy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo_Koy "Jo Koy") hosted the ceremony.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Host-2)

The nominees were announced on December 11, 2023. *[Barbie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbie_(film) "Barbie (film)")* and *[Succession](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Succession_(TV_series) "Succession (TV series)")* both tied for the most nominations with nine each, followed by *[Oppenheimer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oppenheimer_(film) "Oppenheimer (film)")*'s eight.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Nominees-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Barbenheimer-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-11)

The ceremony also featured the debut of two new categories: "[Cinematic and Box Office Achievement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Cinematic_and_Box_Office_Achievement "Golden Globe Award for Cinematic and Box Office Achievement")" and "[Best Performance in Stand-Up Comedy on Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Performance_in_Stand-Up_Comedy_on_Television "Golden Globe Award for Best Performance in Stand-Up Comedy on Television")"[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-New_Categories-12)

Additionally, the cultural phenomenon of "[Barbenheimer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbenheimer "Barbenheimer")" received seventeen nominations, winning seven.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Winners-6)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Barbenheimer-10)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-15)

## Ceremony information

This was the first Golden Globe Awards ceremony after the [Hollywood Foreign Press Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood_Foreign_Press_Association "Hollywood Foreign Press Association") (HFPA) disbanded in 2023. On June 12, 2023, the HFPA announced that all of its rights and properties related to the Golden Globes were acquired by [Dick Clark Productions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Clark_Productions "Dick Clark Productions") and [Eldridge Industries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eldridge_Industries "Eldridge Industries").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-16)

On February 21, 2023, the date of the ceremony was announced. It came back on a Sunday night slot after being moved to Tuesday for the previous year.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Donnelly-4) On September 18, 2023, [Glenn Weiss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glenn_Weiss "Glenn Weiss") and [Ricky Kirshner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ricky_Kirshner "Ricky Kirshner") were announced as its executive producers and showrunners.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Schneider-5) On November 17, 2023, it was announced that [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS") had acquired the broadcast rights to the ceremony, replacing the Golden Globes' long-time U.S. broadcast partner [NBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC "NBC").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Otterson-1)

The nominations were announced on December 11, 2023, during an event co-hosted by [Cedric the Entertainer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cedric_the_Entertainer "Cedric the Entertainer") and [Wilmer Valderrama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilmer_Valderrama "Wilmer Valderrama"). Most of the categories were revealed during a live-streaming presentation, while ten of the categories were revealed during another segment on *[CBS Mornings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS_Mornings "CBS Mornings")*.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Nominees-9)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-18)

On December 21, comedian and actor [Jo Koy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo_Koy "Jo Koy") was announced as the host.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Host-2)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-22) Before this announcement, it was reported that a source with knowledge of the conversations told [CNN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CNN "CNN") that at least five A-list comedic actors, including [Chris Rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Rock "Chris Rock") and [Ali Wong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ali_Wong "Ali Wong"), declined offers to host; the hosts of the podcast *[SmartLess](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SmartLess "SmartLess")* (actors [Will Arnett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Will_Arnett "Will Arnett"), [Jason Bateman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Bateman "Jason Bateman"), and [Sean Hayes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Hayes "Sean Hayes")) also reportedly declined the offer.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-23) That same month, *[TheWrap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TheWrap "TheWrap")* reported that 64 voters threatened to withhold their final-round votes in protest, after being told that they would not be given tickets to the ceremony.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-24)

With the awards no longer being overseen by the HFPA, a new, racially and ethnically diverse group of voters consisting of 300 journalists representing 76 countries selected the 2023 nominees and winners.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Winners_List-7)

For her portrayal of [Mollie Burkhart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mollie_Kyle "Mollie Kyle") in *[Killers of the Flower Moon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Killers_of_the_Flower_Moon "Killers of the Flower Moon")*, [Lily Gladstone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lily_Gladstone "Lily Gladstone") became the first [Indigenous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_Americans_in_the_United_States "Native Americans in the United States") actor to win a Golden Globe Award, winning for [Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Actress_in_a_Motion_Picture_–_Drama "Golden Globe Award for Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Drama").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-25)

### Expansion

On September 26, 2023, it was announced that two new categories would be added for the upcoming ceremony: "[Cinematic and Box Office Achievement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Cinematic_and_Box_Office_Achievement "Golden Globe Award for Cinematic and Box Office Achievement")" (a category for films that grossed at least $100 million domestically and $150 million worldwide) and "[Best Performance in Stand-Up Comedy on Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Performance_in_Stand-Up_Comedy_on_Television "Golden Globe Award for Best Performance in Stand-Up Comedy on Television")" (also known as "Best Stand-Up Comedian on Television").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-New_Categories-12)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-27)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-28)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-29) Some critics felt that the new categories were an attempt to improve the ceremony's viewership and relevance, with comparisons drawn to the [Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards")' [attempt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/91st_Academy_Awards#Proposed_"Popular_Film"_category "91st Academy Awards") to introduce a [category for "Popular Film"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Outstanding_Achievement_in_Popular_Film "Academy Award for Outstanding Achievement in Popular Film") in [2018](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/91st_Academy_Awards "91st Academy Awards").[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-30)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-31)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-32)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-33)

### Reduction

The two Lifetime Achievement Awards (the [Cecil B. DeMille Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Cecil_B._DeMille_Award "Golden Globe Cecil B. DeMille Award") and the [Carol Burnett Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Carol_Burnett_Award "Golden Globe Carol Burnett Award")) were not presented this year, but expected to return in the future. Executive Vice President Tim Gray explained that with the change in ownership and status, and 25 of the competitive categories expanding from 5 nominees to 6, the increase will also include a reduction with no presentation of the two aforementioned awards for this year. "This is not a permanent change, with future awards slated to be given," Gray wrote in a post on the Globes' official website.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-34)

## Reception

### Criticism of Jo Koy's opening monologue

| External videos | |
| --- | --- |
| [![video icon](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1b/Nuvola_apps_kaboodle.svg/20px-Nuvola_apps_kaboodle.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Nuvola_apps_kaboodle.svg) [Jo Koy Opening Monologue \| 81st Annual Golden Globes](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KvSHHnucouo) | |
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/be/Jo_Koy_by_Gage_Skidmore.jpg/250px-Jo_Koy_by_Gage_Skidmore.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Jo_Koy_by_Gage_Skidmore.jpg)[Jo Koy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo_Koy "Jo Koy"), host of the 81st Golden Globe Awards

Host [Jo Koy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo_Koy "Jo Koy")'s opening [monologue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monologue "Monologue") was met with criticism from viewers and critics with many describing his jokes as "cringeworthy", "painful", and "unfunny". Chelsey Sanchez of *[Harper's Bazaar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harper's_Bazaar "Harper's Bazaar")* described the monologue as "awkward" and "distasteful".[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-35) Koy was also criticized for putting blame on his writers during the monologue, coming after the lengthy [2023 Writers Guild of America strike](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Writers_Guild_of_America_strike "2023 Writers Guild of America strike"). Justin Curto of *[Vulture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vulture_(website) "Vulture (website)")* noted that when some of his jokes fell flat, Koy "immediately threw his writers under the bus... He yelled. 'Yo, shut up. You're kidding me, right. Slow down. I wrote some of these and they're the ones you're laughing at'".[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-36) Marlow Stern of *[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone "Rolling Stone")* noted that many of Koy's jokes drew "groans" and "boos" from the audience.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-37)

Among jokes that drew the most ire were those about the film *[Barbie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbie_(film) "Barbie (film)")*, and attending nominees [Robert De Niro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_De_Niro "Robert De Niro"), [Meryl Streep](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meryl_Streep "Meryl Streep") and [Taylor Swift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift "Taylor Swift"); the latter's reaction went viral.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-38)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-39)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-40) Shirley Li of *[The Atlantic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Atlantic "The Atlantic")* wrote: "Practically every joke failed to land, mostly because the punchlines were dated or obvious."[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-41) Nicole Sperling of *[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Times "The New York Times")*, who was in the audience that night, wrote that she had "never seen an audience rebel against an emcee so quickly" and cited a prominent film director describing the monologue as a "disaster".[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-42)

Conversely, four-time [Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards") host and comedian [Whoopi Goldberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whoopi_Goldberg "Whoopi Goldberg") defended Koy on *[The View](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View "The View")*, saying: "These hosting gigs are brutal. They're just brutal. If you don't know the room, if you've not been in these rooms before and you're sort of thrust out there, it's hit or miss. Now, I love Jo Koy, he makes me crazy because he's funny. I don't know whether it was the room, I don't know whether it was the jokes, I didn't get to see it. But I do know, that he is as good as it gets when it comes to stand-ups and it is not an easy gig."[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-43) Actor and comedian [Steve Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Martin "Steve Martin") also threw his support behind Koy on [Threads](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Threads_(social_network) "Threads (social network)"), writing: "I tip my hat to anyone who steps out on stage to host a live awards show. It's a very difficult job and not for the squeamish. I know because I'm still throwing up from the last time I did it in 2010. So, Congratulations to Jo Koy, who took on the toughest gig in show business, hit, missed, was light on his feet, and now has twenty minutes of new material for his stand up!"[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-44)

Additionally, comedian [Michael Che](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Che "Michael Che") supported Koy by writing that "comedians should boycott hosting award shows" on [Instagram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instagram "Instagram").[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-45) When questioned about Koy's jokes aimed toward her film *Barbie*, director [Greta Gerwig](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greta_Gerwig "Greta Gerwig") replied that she was not offended.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-46) On *[Watch What Happens Live with Andy Cohen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Watch_What_Happens_Live_with_Andy_Cohen "Watch What Happens Live with Andy Cohen")*, actor and comedian [Kevin Hart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Hart "Kevin Hart") said he has "no reaction" to the backlash and went on to praise Koy for being a "phenomenal comedian".[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-47) In a [Facebook](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Facebook "Facebook") post by Filipino actor and comedian [Michael V.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_V. "Michael V."), he posted: "I think Jo Koy's Golden Globes jokes are funny, direct, and pretty much self-explanatory. The last thing Jo Koy should be doing is trying to explain it to people who purposely choose NOT to understand and appreciate them."[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-48)

Koy responded to the criticism in an interview with *[Good Morning America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Good_Morning_America "Good Morning America")*, admitting: "I'd be lying if [I said] it doesn't hurt," but also admitted, "I had fun. You know, it was a moment that I'll always remember. Hosting is just a tough gig. Yes, I'm a stand-up comic, but that hosting position it's a different style. I kind of went in and did the writer's thing. We had ten days to write this monologue. It was a crash course. I feel bad, but I got to still say I loved what I did."[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-49) In his first stand-up set afterward, Koy mocked the Hollywood celebrities, alluding: "Lot a marshmallows, man. They're delicious, but goddamn, they're soft. I just come from a different time. I see the changes that are happening. I get it, but goddamn, can we fucking laugh at ourselves?"[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-50)

The **82nd Golden Globe Awards** was an awards ceremony that honored [excellence in film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_in_film "2024 in film") and [American television productions of 2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_in_American_television "2024 in American television"). The winners were revealed during the live telecast, airing on [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS") and streaming on [Paramount+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramount+ "Paramount+") on January 5, 2025.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-2) The event was hosted by comedian [Nikki Glaser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikki_Glaser "Nikki Glaser"), making her the first solo female host in Golden Globes history.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Glaser-3)

The nominations were announced live on December 9, 2024, at a [press conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Press_conference "Press conference") at [the Beverly Hilton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Beverly_Hilton "The Beverly Hilton") by actors [Morris Chestnut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morris_Chestnut "Morris Chestnut") and [Mindy Kaling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mindy_Kaling "Mindy Kaling"), following an introduction from Golden Globes president, Helen Hoenhe.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Globes-4) *[Emilia Pérez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emilia_Pérez "Emilia Pérez")*, with 10 nominations, became the most nominated comedy/musical film in [Golden Globes history](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Awards#Superlatives "Golden Globe Awards"), just 1 shy of the overall record of 11, set by [Robert Altman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Altman "Robert Altman")'s [country music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_music "Country music") [satire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satire_(film_and_television) "Satire (film and television)") *[Nashville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nashville_(film) "Nashville (film)")* in the drama category in [1976](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/33rd_Golden_Globe_Awards "33rd Golden Globe Awards").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-5) *[The Brutalist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist "The Brutalist")* received the second-most in film with 7 nominations, followed by *[Conclave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conclave_(film) "Conclave (film)")* with 6.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-6) Additionally, *[The Bear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series) "The Bear (TV series)")* led the television nominations with 5, followed by *[Only Murders in the Building](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Only_Murders_in_the_Building "Only Murders in the Building")* and *[Shōgun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shōgun_(2024_TV_series) "Shōgun (2024 TV series)")* with 4 each.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Variety-7)

## Ceremony information

On August 28, 2024, comedian [Nikki Glaser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikki_Glaser "Nikki Glaser") was announced as the host for this year's ceremony, following last year's widely criticized host, comedian [Jo Koy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo_Koy "Jo Koy").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Glaser-3) She is the first woman to host the Golden Globes solo.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-8) Glaser herself was nominated for [Best Performance in Stand-Up Comedy on Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Performance_in_Stand-Up_Comedy_on_Television "Golden Globe Award for Best Performance in Stand-Up Comedy on Television") for her [HBO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HBO "HBO") comedy special, *Nikki Glaser: Someday You'll Die*,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Governors-9) but lost to [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix")'s *Ali Wong: Single Lady*.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-10)

The ceremony was held at 5:00 p.m. [PST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Time_Zone "Pacific Time Zone") / 8:00 p.m. [EST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Time_Zone "Eastern Time Zone") on January 5, 2025. It was broadcast live on [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS") and streamed on [Paramount+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramount+ "Paramount+").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Globes-4) [Glenn Weiss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glenn_Weiss "Glenn Weiss") and [Ricky Kirshner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ricky_Kirshner "Ricky Kirshner") of White Cherry Entertainment returned from last year to executive produce the ceremony, along with [Dick Clark Productions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Clark_Productions "Dick Clark Productions").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Globes-4)

On December 3, 2024, it was announced that the two Lifetime Achievement Awards, which were not presented last year, would return this year; however, they were presented during an untelevised gala dinner on January 3, 2025, prior to the telecast, similar to the [Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards")' [Governors Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governors_Awards "Governors Awards").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Governors-9) The recipient of the [Cecil B. DeMille Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Cecil_B._DeMille_Award "Golden Globe Cecil B. DeMille Award") was [Viola Davis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viola_Davis "Viola Davis"), while the [Carol Burnett Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Carol_Burnett_Award "Golden Globe Carol Burnett Award") was awarded to [Ted Danson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_Danson "Ted Danson").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-11)

*[Emilia Pérez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emilia_Pérez "Emilia Pérez")* star [Karla Sofía Gascón](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karla_Sofía_Gascón "Karla Sofía Gascón") was the first [trans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transgender "Transgender") nominee for a Golden Globe motion picture acting category, for the [Best Actress in a Musical or Comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Actress_in_a_Motion_Picture_–_Musical_or_Comedy "Golden Globe Award for Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy") category.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-12) [Jacques Audiard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacques_Audiard "Jacques Audiard"), the director and writer of the film, was one of the most nominated individuals, with a total of three nominations: [Best Director](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Director "Golden Globe Award for Best Director"), [Best Screenplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Screenplay "Golden Globe Award for Best Screenplay"), and co-lyricist of [Best Original Song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Original_Song "Golden Globe Award for Best Original Song") nominee "[El Mal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El_Mal_(song) "El Mal (song)")".[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Variety-7) The composers and co-lyricists of the song, [Camille](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camille_(French_singer) "Camille (French singer)") and [Clément Ducol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clément_Ducol "Clément Ducol"), tied Audiard for most nominated individuals. Aside from "El Mal", they were also jointly nominated for composing *Emilia Pérez*'s [Best Original Score](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Original_Score "Golden Globe Award for Best Original Score") and an additional Best Original Song nominee: "[Mi camino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mi_camino "Mi camino")".[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Variety-7)

This year's nominations were tabulated by [KPMG](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KPMG "KPMG"), the U.S. audit, tax, and advisory firm, taking over [Ernst & Young](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ernst_&_Young "Ernst & Young") after fifty plus years.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Globes-4)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-15) [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix") received a total of 36 nominations between film and television, the most of any distributor.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-16)

*Emilia Pérez* is the first non-English-language film (with some parts of English in the film) to win [Best Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Motion_Picture_–_Musical_or_Comedy "Golden Globe Award for Best Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy"). *[Flow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flow_(2024_film) "Flow (2024 film)")* is the first [Latvian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latvian_language "Latvian language") film to win [Best Animated Feature Film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Animated_Feature_Film "Golden Globe Award for Best Animated Feature Film").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-17) [Fernanda Torres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fernanda_Torres "Fernanda Torres") became the first [Brazilian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazilian_Portuguese "Brazilian Portuguese") actress to win a Golden Globe in an acting category,[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Torres-18) as well as the first Brazilian, first [South American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_America "South America") and first [Portuguese-speaking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_language "Portuguese language") actor to win the [Golden Globe Award for Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Actress_in_a_Motion_Picture_–_Drama "Golden Globe Award for Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Drama").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Torres-18) She acknowledged her mother [Fernanda Montenegro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fernanda_Montenegro "Fernanda Montenegro")'s nomination, for *[Central Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Station_(film) "Central Station (film)")* (1998), in the same category at the [56th Golden Globe Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/56th_Golden_Globe_Awards "56th Golden Globe Awards").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Torres-18)

*Emilia Pérez* and *[Shōgun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shōgun_(2024_TV_series) "Shōgun (2024 TV series)")* were the biggest winners of the night, for film and television, respectively, with four wins each.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Winners-19) *[The Brutalist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist "The Brutalist")* was the next biggest film recipient, with three wins; for television, *[Baby Reindeer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baby_Reindeer "Baby Reindeer")* and *[Hacks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hacks_(TV_series) "Hacks (TV series)")* each won two.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Winners-19)

# 81st Golden Globe Award Nominations: Here’s the Full List

![](https://observer.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2023/12/GettyImages-1363723613.jpg?quality=80)Golden Globes are seen during the 79th Annual Golden Globe Awards. Photo by Emma McIntyre/Getty Images for Hollywood Foreign Press Association

The Golden Globes have undergone plenty of changes in the past year, from turning into a for-profit company to moving their longtime broadcast home to CBS, but the perennial awards show is still the place to be for awards hopefuls. Though this awards season’s cycle has been disrupted by the WGA and SAG strikes, the Globes remain one of the first red carpet stops on the glitzy path to glory.

Nominations for both film and television awards were announced earlier this morning via CBS News and are listed below. The 81st Golden Globes will be broadcast by CBS (and stream on Paramount+) on Sunday, January 7th.

# Golden Globe Nominations: Surprises and Snubs to Start Awards Season

![](https://observer.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2023/12/GettyImages-1363723613.jpg?quality=80&w=970)Golden Globes are seen during the 79th Annual Golden Globe Awards. Photo by Emma McIntyre/Getty Images for Hollywood Foreign Press Association

‘Tis the season—of awards. And while a fair number of organizations and associations have already announced their nominations and best picture picks, the Golden Globes still serve as a major, if not *the* major, preliminary awards show. Despite controversies and network changes, the Globes seem to be on an upward trajectory, with another batch of eclectic nominations. Films like *Emilia Pérez*, *The Brutalist*, [*Conclave*](https://observer.com/2024/10/conclave-review-papal-succession-as-a-mystery-thriller/), *The Substance* and [*Anora*](https://observer.com/2024/10/anora-review-one-of-the-funniest-saddest-best-films-of-the-year/)lead in nominations, and on the TV end things look pretty business-as-usual with *The Bear*, *Shogun*, and *Only Murders in the Building* making the biggest impact. That said, there are some good surprises (as well as some shocking snubs) too.

The 82nd Golden Globes will be held on Sunday, January 5th. The show will air on CBS and stream on Paramount+ starting at 8pm ET, with comedian [Nikki Glaser](https://observer.com/person/nikki-glaser/ "Nikki Glaser") hosting the affair.

[https://www.youtube.com/embed/LNlrGhBpYjc?feature=oembed](https://www.youtube.com/embed/LNlrGhBpYjc?feature=oembed)

### **Surprise: Female directors break through**

Ignoring women behind the camera has long been a problem for awards bodies, but for the second year in a row (and third time overall) the Globes have nominated two women for Best Director. They are [Coralie Fargeat](https://observer.com/person/coralie-fargeat/ "Coralie Fargeat"), with her popular feminist body horror flick *The Substance* (which also earned nominations for actress [Demi Moore](https://observer.com/person/demi-moore/ "Demi Moore") and supporting actress [Margaret Qualley](https://observer.com/person/margaret-qualley/ "Margaret Qualley")), and [Payal Kapadia](https://observer.com/person/payal-kapadia/ "Payal Kapadia"), whose *All We Imagine as Light* is also nominated for Best Motion Picture: Non-English Language. The latter has an uncertain road ahead of her for this awards season, given that *All We Imagine* was not submitted by any country for the Oscars, but it’s wonderful to see the Golden Globes recognizing Kapadia’s moving work.

### **Snub: No Saoirse Ronan**

It’s been pretty much assumed that 2024 could finally be [Saoirse Ronan](https://observer.com/person/saoirse-ronan/ "Saoirse Ronan")’s year to come out on top—with stirring performances in two well-received films, it was more a question of how many nominations she would get, not whether she would receive any at all. Yet the Globes chose to pass her over, with her moving portrayal of a recovering alcoholic in *The Outrun* left out of lead actress contention and her supporting work in [*Blitz*](https://observer.com/2024/10/bfi-london-film-festival-premiere-steve-mcqueens-blitz/)being ignored. It’ll be interesting to see how she fares the further the season goes on.

![](https://observer.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2024/12/image7.jpg?quality=80&w=970)Director John M. Chu, Cynthia Erivo, and Ariana Grande on the set of *Wicked*. [Courtesy of Universal Pictures](https://www.wickedmovie.com/gallery/)

### **Surprise:** ***Wicked*** **is not the most-nominated musical**

The Golden Globes, with their Musical/Comedy categories and general appreciation for flashier titles, seemed like the perfect place to kick off *Wicked*’s awards season run, with many prognosticators looking to [John M. Chu](https://observer.com/person/john-m-chu/ "John M. Chu")’s blockbuster as a major player. However, the movie musical only ended up with four nominations, including Best Picture, Best Actress for [Cynthia Erivo](https://observer.com/person/cynthia-erivo/ "Cynthia Erivo"), and Best Supporting Actress for [Ariana Grande](https://observer.com/person/ariana-grande/ "Ariana Grande").

*Wicked* faced significant musical competition thanks to *Emilia Pérez*, which racked up 10 total nominations. The Spanish-language film from French director [Jacques Audiard](https://observer.com/person/jacques-audiard/ "Jacques Audiard") earned the second most nominations ever, trailing [Robert Altman](https://observer.com/person/robert-altman/ "Robert Altman")’s country music epic *Nashville* by one. Notably, the movie doubled up in multiple categories, with two nominations for Best Original Song and both [Selena Gomez](https://observer.com/person/selena-gomez/ "Selena Gomez") and Zoe Saldaña getting nominated for Best Supporting Actress. *Emilia Pérez* might not be everyone’s cup of tea, but the Globes clearly loved it.

### **Snub:** ***Kneecap*** **gets, well, kneecapped**

The Irish can’t seem to catch a break this year! After winning seven awards at the British Independent Film Awards just this weekend, *Kneecap* got completely shut out of the Globes. The film, which tells the story of the Belfast-based, Irish language hip-hop group Kneecap, was heavily favored to break into the Non-English Language category, and it seemed plausible that the madcap movie could find space in the Musical/Comedy categories too. Unfortunately, *Kneecap* didn’t resonate with Golden Globes members.

![](https://observer.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2024/11/GL2_29680RC2_rgb.jpg?quality=80&w=970)Denzel Washington plays Macrinus in *Gladiator II* from Paramount Pictures. Cuba Scott/Courtesy of Paramount Pictures

### **Surprise: Blockbusters don’t really make the cut**

The year after “Barbenheimer” and the introduction of the Globes’ Cinematic and Box Office Achievement Award, it seemed like the Golden Globes would once again be a prime place for big movies to be rewarded. Not only would *Wicked* be huge, but [*Gladiator II*](https://observer.com/2024/11/gladiator-ii-review-compelling-ridiculous-and-uproariously-pleasurable/), [*Deadpool & Wolverine*](https://observer.com/2024/07/deadpool-wolverine-review-crowd-pleasing-pops-no-substance/), and [*Beetlejuice Beetlejuice*](https://observer.com/2024/09/beetlejuice-beetlejuice-review-pure-genuine-fun-and-occasionally-gross/) all seemed like they had opportunities to break into big categories. But sadly (or luckily, if you’re among the more proudly pretentious among us), this was not to be.

*Gladiator II* only received one nomination outside of the nebulous Cinematic and Box Office Achievement category, a nod for [Denzel Washington](https://observer.com/person/denzel-washington/ "Denzel Washington")’s supporting performance. Meanwhile, [*Dune: Part Two*](https://observer.com/2024/02/dune-part-two-review-part-stunning-epic-part-pulpy-space-opera/) somehow missed out on the box office category despite being the fourth highest grossing movie of the year, but got nominated for Best Score and Best Motion Picture Drama. Maybe the real surprise of the ceremony will be learning what Cinematic and Box Office Achievement actually means!

### **Snub: Hard truths for** ***Hard Truths***

Despite making an impact with the British Independent Film Awards, the New York Film Critics Circle, the Los Angeles Film Critics Association, and the National Board of Review, [Mike Leigh](https://observer.com/person/mike-leigh/ "Mike Leigh")’s independent drama *Hard Truths* failed to make a splash at the Golden Globes. Lead actress [Marianne Jean-Baptiste](https://observer.com/person/marianne-jean-baptiste/ "Marianne Jean-Baptiste") has already won awards for her performance as the depressed and sometimes darkly funny Pansy, marking her as one to watch this season, but the Globes don’t seem to agree with those accolades.

![](https://observer.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2024/12/MONSTERS_206_Unit_07247RC.jpg?quality=80&w=970)(L-R) Nicholas Chavez as Lyle Menendez, Cooper Koch as Erik Menendez, and Javier Bardem as Jose Menendez in *Monsters: The Lyle And Erik Menendez Story*. MILES CRIST/NETFLIX

### **Surprise: Ryan Murphy sees success**

Ok, sure, it’s not *really* a surprise that the Golden Globes are highlighting [Ryan Murphy](https://observer.com/person/ryan-murphy/ "Ryan Murphy")’s biggest show of the year with three major nominations for *Monsters: The Lyle and Erik Menendez Story*. You’d be hard pressed to find a creative that the organization responds to better than Murphy, regardless of the quality of some of his projects (including this one). Good for undeniable breakout star [Cooper Koch](https://observer.com/person/cooper-koch/ "Cooper Koch"), though, who faces some really stiff competition in the Best Actor in a Limited Series category.

### **Snub: No love for Clarence Maclin**

Another unfortunate exclusion belongs to [*Sing Sing*](https://observer.com/2024/07/sing-sing-review-a24s-moving-film-about-the-power-of-art-behind-bars/?preview_id=1431643&_thumbnail_id=1431648)’s [Clarence Maclin](https://observer.com/person/clarence-maclin/ "Clarence Maclin"), whose soulful supporting performance ranks among the best of the year. This indie film about the titular prison’s Rehabilitation Through the Arts program only nabbed one nomination, for its star [Colman Domingo](https://observer.com/person/colman-domingo/ "Colman Domingo"), but Maclin has been tapped as a welcome nominee by the Independent Spirit Awards, and he won at the Gotham Awards earlier this month. As with Saoirse Ronan and Marianne Jean-Baptiste, this loss could signal a bumpy awards run ahead.

![](https://observer.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2024/12/Squidgame_Unit_204_N064080.jpg?quality=80&w=970)Lee Jung-jae as Seong Gi-hun in *Squid Game* Season 2. No Ju-han/Netflix

### **Surprise:** ***Squid Game*** **is back!**

We’re used to movies racking up nominations before they’re widely available to see, but television rarely takes the same route. Leave it to *Squid Game* to break the mold again, as it’s earned a nomination for Best Television Series: Drama more than two weeks before it’s due to be released on Netflix. That is the only nod that the ultra-popular Korean series received, with no acting nominations to tip interested parties off on who the major players in Season 2 might be.

| Data | 7 de dezembro de 2023 |
| Local | [Peacock Theater](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft_Theater "Microsoft Theater") ([Los Angeles](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles"), [Califórnia](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Califórnia "Califórnia")) |

| [Página oficial](http://thegameawards.com/) | |

**The Game Awards 2023** foi a décima cerimônia de premiação anual do [The Game Awards](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards "The Game Awards"), na qual homenageou os melhores [jogos eletrônicos](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jogo_eletrônico "Jogo eletrônico") de [2023](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023 "2023"). Foi apresentada por [Geoff Keighley](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geoff_Keighley "Geoff Keighley"), criador e produtor da cerimônia, e realizada ao vivo para um público no [Peacock Theater](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft_Theater "Microsoft Theater") em Los Angeles no dia 7 de dezembro de 2023, bem como [transmitida ao vivo](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_streaming "Live streaming"). O pré-show foi apresentado por Sydnee Goodman. O evento contou com apresentações musicais de Loren Allred, Heilung e [Old Gods of Asgard](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Gods_of_Asgard "Old Gods of Asgard"), além de participações especiais de celebridades como [Timothée Chalamet](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timothée_Chalamet "Timothée Chalamet"), [Christopher Judge](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Judge "Christopher Judge") e [Matthew McConaughey](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matthew_McConaughey "Matthew McConaughey").

*[Baldur's Gate III](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baldur's_Gate_III "Baldur's Gate III")* liderou a premiação com nove indicações e seis vitórias, incluindo [Jogo do Ano](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Award_de_Jogo_do_Ano "The Game Award de Jogo do Ano") e "Melhor Performance" para Neil Newbon. Vários novos jogos foram anunciados durante o evento, incluindo *[Marvel's Blade](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marvel's_Blade_(futuro_jogo_eletrônico) "Marvel's Blade (futuro jogo eletrônico)")*, *Lost Records: Bloom & Rage* e *Visions of Mana*. A cerimônia foi vista por mais de 118 milhões de pessoas, o maior recorde da sua história, com mais de 17.000 transmissões simultâneas de criadores de conteúdo. Alguns jornalistas criticaram o evento por priorizar anúncios e celebridades em vez das premiações, além da não reconhecer as demissões na indústria e ignorar a [crise humanitária na Faixa de Gaza](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crise_humanitária_em_Gaza_(2023-presente) "Crise humanitária em Gaza (2023-presente)").

## Vencedores e indicados

Os indicados foram anunciados em 13 de novembro de 2023.[[2]](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Variety_Nominees-2) Qualquer jogo lançado para consumo público até 17 de novembro de 2023 era considerado elegível. Os indicados foram compilados por um júri composto por membros de mais de 100 meios de comunicação de todo o mundo. Júris especializados decidiram os indicados para categorias como acessibilidade, adaptação e [esporte eletrônico](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Esporte_eletrônico "Esporte eletrônico").[[3]](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-FAQ-3) Os vencedores são determinados entre o júri (90% de impacto nos resultados finais) e a votação do público (10%); este último é realizado através do site oficial e no servidor [Discord](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discord "Discord")[[a]](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-5) até 6 de dezembro.[[4]](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Kotaku_Nominees-4)[[5]](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-PC_Gamer_Nominees-6) A exceção é o prêmio "Voz dos Jogadores", que é totalmente nomeado e votado pelo público, com a votação sendo aberta em 27 de novembro.[[6]](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Push_Square_Voice-7) De acordo com Keighley, a votação no site no primeiro dia teve um aumento de 73% em relação ao ano anterior.[[7]](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Variety_Interview-8)

O The Game Awards fez uma parceria com a Nighttimes e a Studio 568 para criar um mundo central dentro do jogo *[Fortnite](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fortnite "Fortnite")*. Disponível a partir de 14 de novembro, esse hub permitiu que os jogadores votassem em suas ilhas favoritas criadas por usuários entre dez indicados; o vencedor foi anunciado durante a cerimônia. Keighley vinha buscando criar mais eventos dentro de jogos desde que apresentou um show ao vivo no *Fortnite* em 2019.[[8]](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Destructoid_Fortnite-9)[[9]](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-VentureBeat_Fortnite-10) Ele pretende possibilitar a visualização ao vivo do The Game Awards dentro do jogo no futuro, considerando esse método de publicidade mais eficaz do que o marketing tradicional, como *[outdoors](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outdoors "Outdoors")*. De acordo com Keighley, o hub central ultrapassou um milhão de acessos em três dias, contando com mais de 875.000 jogadores únicos.[[10]](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Keighley_Fortnite-11)

### Categorias

# The Game Awards 2023 Winners: The Full List

The Game Awards 2023 has ended, but not before it treated us to a celebration of the past and future of the world of gaming. While The Game Awards was filled with big reveals and news about upcoming games, it also obviously honored the incredible games and developers from the past year.

This article will gather all the big winners of the night, including the coveted Game of the Year award which, in [the behemoth that was 2023,](https://www.google.com/url?sa=t&rct=j&q=&esrc=s&source=web&cd=&ved=2ahUKEwix-fXchf-CAxU4kYkEHUKyD3sQFnoECBUQAQ&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.ign.com%2Farticles%2Fbest-reviewed-games-of-2023&usg=AOvVaw1R1ie4c0IqKbK__v3J1rMZ&opi=89978449) is even more special. While this year was filled with games that all could have won Game of the Year in other years, only one could walk away with the award and this time it was Baldur's Gate 3.

Not only did Baldur's Gate 3 win Game of the Year and [shadow drop its Xbox version,](https://www.ign.com/articles/baldurs-gate-3-is-now-available-on-xbox-series-xs) but it also won Best Community Support, Best RPG, Best Multiplayer, and the Player's Voice category. Alan Wake 2 followed with 3 wins in the categories of Best Game Direction, Best Narrative, and Best Art Direction.

You can check out the full list of The Game Awards 2023 winners below, and also be sure to check out [our roundup of all the biggest reveals from The Game Awards!](https://www.ign.com/articles/the-game-awards-2023-everything-announced)

### **Game of the Year**

*Recognizing a game that delivers the absolute best experience across all creative and technical fields.*

Let's open the arXiv page for details. Use page_scraper on https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.12049.

The arXiv page doesn't list authors directly in the snippet. We need to find author list. Usually arXiv abstract page has authors at top, but maybe not captured by scraper. Let's try to get the HTML version or look for "Authors" section. Use page_scraper on the html link: https://arxiv.org/html/2410.12049v4? Or just search within. Could also use search query "Sabiá-3 Technical Report authors". Let's open the researchgate link or emergentmind. But better to find Google Scholar entry.

# [2410.12049] Sabiá-3 Technical Report

[View PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2410.12049) [HTML (experimental)](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.12049v4)
> Abstract:This report presents Sabiá-3, our new flagship language model, and Sabiazinho-3, a more cost-effective sibling. The models were trained on a large brazilian-centric corpus. Evaluations across diverse professional and academic benchmarks show a strong performance on Portuguese and Brazil-related tasks. Sabiá-3 shows large improvements in comparison to our previous best of model, Sabia-2 Medium, especially in reasoning-intensive tasks. Notably, Sabiá-3's average performance matches frontier LLMs, while it is offered at a three to four times lower cost per token, reinforcing the benefits of domain specialization.

# Sabiá-3 Technical Report

- The paper demonstrates cost-effective LLM specialization through refinement with culturally enriched Brazilian Portuguese data and human-guided post-training.
- It details a two-phase methodology combining self-supervised pre-training and annotation-enhanced tuning for precise instruction adherence.
- Evaluations reveal robust conversational, function-calling, and long-context processing abilities, with noted areas for improvement in multi-turn tasks.

## Analysis of the Sabiá-3 Technical Report

The technical report delineates the development, training, and evaluation of Sabiá-3 and Sabiazinho-3, a new line of LLMs optimized for Brazilian Portuguese and culturally specific tasks. This meticulous effort endeavors to demonstrate the proficiency and economic benefits of domain specialization in natural language processing.

### Model Development and Training

The development of Sabiá-3 pivots on continual learning principles, leveraging an initial generalist model and further refining it using a corpus enriched with Brazilian Portuguese content. This corpus is curated to capture not only the linguistic structure but also the sociocultural contexts pertinent to Brazil. The training process is bifurcated into two major phases: a pre-training phase involving self-supervised [next-token prediction](https://www.emergentmind.com/topics/next-token-prediction-ntp "") on a high-quality, voluminous corpus, and a post-training phase where human annotations and synthetic data guide the model in instruction adherence and [preference alignment](https://www.emergentmind.com/topics/preference-alignment "").

The scale of data collection has notably progressed from previous iterations, with methodical enhancements implemented in data quality filtration. Training efficiency is bolstered by the utilization of [TPU](https://www.emergentmind.com/topics/tensor-processing-unit-tpu "") v5 hardware, adopting [data and model parallelism](https://www.emergentmind.com/topics/data-and-model-parallelism "") strategies.

### Evaluation and Performance

#### Multiple-choice Exam Performance

Empirical evaluations substantiate that Sabiá-3 and Sabiazinho-3 excel in handling Portuguese language tasks, particularly those requiring intricate reasoning capabilities. Assessments involving 96 diverse academic exams yield a formidable performance relative to competing LLMs, with Sabiá-3 achieving parity with leading [generalist models](https://www.emergentmind.com/topics/generalist-models "") like [GPT-4o](https://www.emergentmind.com/topics/vocabulary-assistant-llm-gpt-4o "") at a significantly reduced operational cost.

Sabiá-3's accuracy in knowledge-intensive tasks, such as the National Student Performance Exam and Unified National Public Competition, attests to its adeptness in domain-specific scenarios. Despite these advancements, there remain challenges in select disciplines, which provide a pathway for ongoing enhancement.

#### Conversational and Instruction-following Capabilities

The Brazilian Chat Evaluation (BRACEval) highlights Sabiá-3's conversational proficiency, where its performance closely resembles that of top-tier models in dialogic engagements. However, opportunities for growth lie in improving alignment with instruction-following tasks, as illustrated by IFEval benchmark results that position Sabiá-3 behind its competitors.

#### Function Calling and Long Context Processing

In terms of executing function calls and contextual comprehension, Sabiá-3 shows commendable function-calling accuracy, though it requires further refinement in multi-turn and multi-step task management. The Portuguese adaptation of the Needle-in-the-Haystack benchmark reflects Sabiá-3's robust capacity for handling extended textual inputs, suggesting its potential for expanded contextual reasoning tasks.

#### Agentic Capabilities

Evaluations using [AgentBench](https://www.emergentmind.com/topics/agentbench "") illuminate the model's competencies in agentic tasks, particularly in web-grounded environments. However, there is room for progression in code-related tasks, aligning with the broader trend of [LLM-based agents](https://www.emergentmind.com/topics/llm-based-agents "") taking on increasingly complex, multi-disciplinary roles.

### Implications and Future Directions

The report underscores the viability and cost-effectiveness of specialization in LLM development, challenging the predominantly generalized approach. Sabiá-3 serves as a testament to the merits of customizing LLMs to tailormade domains, which may outstrip generalist models in context-specific tasks.

Future endeavors should focus on refining instruction-following precision, optimizing capacities for multi-step action execution, and broadening the model's scope in multilingual functionality. Expanding these capabilities will not only fortify Sabiá-3's applicability across diverse use cases but also enhance its competitive standing in a rapidly evolving landscape of LLMs.

The Sabiá-3 initiative marks a pivotal advancement in developing LLMs tuned to specific linguistic and cultural demands, paving the way for analogous endeavors across other linguistic and regional [spectra](https://www.emergentmind.com/topics/spectra-6815ea26-e478-4301-bbaa-6afdedfa981b "").

Reranking plays a crucial role in improving Information Retrieval (IR) performance, particularly in low-resource languages, such as Portuguese. In this study, we evaluate different reranking strategies for Portuguese IR, comparing multilingual and Portuguese-specific models, as well as not-so-large language models and large language models (LLMs). We assess the performance of BM25 combined with ptT5 fine-tuned on multilingual and Brazilian Portuguese datasets, alongside multilingual state-of-the-art rerankers (BGE m3) and LLM as rerankers RankGPT (GPT-4) and Sabiá 3, a Portuguese-specific LLM. Additionally, we introduce a novel dynamic In-Context Learning (DICL) prompting strategy to enhance LLM performance. Experiments conducted on the Quati and Pirá 2.0 datasets show that fine-tuning on native Brazilian Portuguese data significantly improves retrieval effectiveness by up to 5 p.p. in nDCG compared to using translated multilingual datasets. Two fine-tuning approaches were tested: a binary classification strategy with ‘true’ and ‘false’ tokens and a relevance score-based training, both outperforming models fine-tuned on translated multilingual data. RankGPT achieved the best overall results, yet Sabiá 3 demonstrated competitive performance, particularly on queries related to sociocultural aspects. The DICL strategy further improved the results of both LLMs, significantly boosting their MRR@10. These findings highlight the importance of language-specific training and suggest that not-so-large language models can be viable alternatives for reranking tasks in Portuguese IR.

This study evaluates the performance of Large Language Models (LLMs) in predicting ratings for Brazilian Portuguese user reviews. We benchmark ten LLMs, including ChatGPT-3.5, ChatGPT-4o, DeepSeek, Mistral, LLaMA (3, 3.3), Gemma (1, 2), and the Brazilian Portuguese-specific models Sabiá-3 and Sabiazinho, using two prompting strategies: simple (p1) and detailed (p2). Results indicate that ChatGPT-4o and DeepSeek achieved the highest accuracy, particularly in predicting extreme ratings (1 and 5 stars). Sabiá-3 also performed competitively, highlighting the potential of language-specific models. Models performed better in objective categories such as food and baby products but struggled with more subjective domains like automotive and games. Cost analysis showed that DeepSeek is a more cost-effective alternative to ChatGPT-4o while maintaining similar accuracy. This study provides a systematic benchmark of LLMs for rating prediction in Brazilian Portuguese, offering insights into their effectiveness and limitations.

In Artificial Intelligence (AI), language models have gained significant importance due to the widespread adoption of systems capable of simulating realistic conversations with humans through text generation. Because of their impact on society, developing and deploying these language models must be done responsibly, with attention to their negative impacts and possible harms. In this scenario, the number of AI Ethics Tools (AIETs) publications has recently increased. These AIETs are designed to help developers, companies, governments, and other stakeholders establish trust, transparency, and responsibility with their technologies by bringing accepted values to guide AI's design, development, and use stages. However, many AIETs lack good documentation, examples of use, and proof of their effectiveness in practice. This paper presents a methodology for evaluating AIETs in language models. Our approach involved an extensive literature survey on 213 AIETs, and after applying inclusion and exclusion criteria, we selected four AIETs: Model Cards, ALTAI, FactSheets, and Harms Modeling. For evaluation, we applied AIETs to language models developed for the Portuguese language, conducting 35 hours of interviews with their developers. The evaluation considered the developers' perspective on the AIETs' use and quality in helping to identify ethical considerations about their model. The results suggest that the applied AIETs serve as a guide for formulating general ethical considerations about language models. However, we note that they do not address unique aspects of these models, such as idiomatic expressions. Additionally, these AIETs did not help to identify potential negative impacts of models for the Portuguese language.

This study presents an extensive comparative analysis of Large Language Models (LLMs) for sentiment analysis in Brazilian Portuguese texts. We evaluated 23 LLMs—comprising 13 state-of-the-art multilingual models and 10 models specifically fine-tuned for Portuguese—across 12 public annotated datasets from diverse domains, employing the in-context learning paradigm. Our findings demonstrate that large-scale models such as Claude-3.5-Sonnet, GPT-4o, DeepSeek-V3, and Sabiá-3 delivered superior results with accuracies exceeding 92%, while smaller models (7-13B parameters) also showed compelling performance with top performers achieving accuracies above 90%. Notably, linguistic specialization through fine-tuning demonstrated mixed results—significantly reducing hallucination rates for some models but not consistently yielding performance improvements across all model types. We also observed that newer model generations frequently outperformed their predecessors, and in the one dataset where traditional machine learning methods were employed by the original authors for sentiment classification, all evaluated LLMs substantially surpassed these traditional approaches. Moreover, smaller-scale models exhibited a tendency toward overgeneration despite explicit instructions. These findings contribute valuable insights to the discourse on language-specific model optimization and establish empirical benchmarks for both multilingual and Portuguese-specialized LLMs in sentiment analysis tasks.

The growth of social media in the present decade is one of the main drivers of studies on user-generated content. Reddit, a social network that has been gaining popularity among Brazilians, has become a source for sentiment analysis studies aimed at evaluating automated models for this task. This article reports a study on the development and evaluation of a dataset of human-annotated Reddit comments and its comparison with sentiment classification models. Comments retrieved from Brazilian Reddit communities were labeled by annotators and submitted to automated classification using 10 models with different architectures. Human labeling showed moderate agreement coefficients and reasonable disagreement, highlighting the subjectivity of the task. Models based on LLMs and BERT performed well with Brazilian Portuguese texts. The comparison revealed similarities in the challenges faced by humans and models, suggesting opportunities to improve automated language understanding. Both humans and models face similar difficulties in sentiment assignment, language characteristics of the texts being a major challenge for model classification, which points to the need for further advancement in this respect.

- [Jhessica Silva](https://www.researchgate.net/scientific-contributions/Jhessica-Silva-2268387703)
- [Diego A. B. Moreira](https://www.researchgate.net/scientific-contributions/Diego-A-B-Moreira-2344915464)
- [Gabriel Oliveira dos SantosGabriel Oliveira dos Santos](https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Gabriel-Oliveira-Dos-Santos-2)
- [Helio Pedrini](https://www.researchgate.net/scientific-contributions/Helio-Pedrini-2245741163)

In Artificial Intelligence (AI), language models have gained significant importance due to the widespread adoption of systems capable of simulating realistic conversations with humans through text generation. Because of their impact on society, developing and deploying these language models must be done responsibly, with attention to their negative impacts and possible harms. In this scenario, the number of AI Ethics Tools (AIETs) publications has recently increased. These AIETs are designed to help developers, companies, governments, and other stakeholders establish trust, transparency, and responsibility with their technologies by bringing accepted values to guide AI’s design, development, and use stages. However, many AIETs lack good documentation, examples of use, and proof of their effectiveness in practice. This paper presents a methodology for evaluating AIETs in language models. Our approach involved an extensive literature survey on 213 AIETs, and after applying inclusion and exclusion criteria, we selected four AIETs: Model Cards, ALTAI, FactSheets, and Harms Modeling. For evaluation, we applied AIETs to language models developed for the Portuguese language, conducting 35 h of interviews with their developers. The evaluation considered the developers’ perspective on the AIETs’ use and quality in helping to identify ethical considerations about their model. The results suggest that the applied AIETs serve as a guide for formulating general ethical considerations about language models. However, we note that they do not address unique aspects of these models, such as idiomatic expressions. Additionally, these AIETs did not help to identify potential negative impacts of models for the Portuguese language.

- [Leandro Carísio FernandesLeandro Carísio Fernandes](https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Leandro-Fernandes-7)

This paper introduces JurisTCU, a Brazilian Portuguese dataset for legal information retrieval (LIR). The dataset is freely available (https://huggingface.co/datasets/LeandroRibeiro/JurisTCU) and consists of 16,045 jurisprudential documents from the Brazilian Federal Court of Accounts, along with 150 queries annotated with relevance judgments. It addresses the scarcity of Portuguese-language LIR datasets with query relevance annotations. The queries are organized into three groups: real user keyword-based queries, synthetic keyword-based queries, and synthetic question-based queries. Relevance judgments were produced through a hybrid approach combining LLM-based scoring with expert domain validation. We used JurisTCU in 14 experiments using lexical search (document expansion methods) and semantic search (BERT-based and OpenAI embeddings). We show that the document expansion methods significantly improve the performance of standard BM25 search on this dataset, with improvements exceeding 45% in P@10, R@10, and nDCG@10 metrics when evaluating short keyword-based queries. Among the embedding models, the OpenAI models produced the best results, with improvements of approximately 70% in P@10, R@10, and nDCG@10 metrics for short keyword-based queries, suggesting that these dense embeddings capture semantic relationships in this domain, surpassing the reliance on lexical terms. Besides offering a dataset for the Portuguese-language IR research community, suitable for evaluating search systems, the results also contribute to enhancing a search system highly relevant to Brazilian citizens.

- [Ricardo da Silva SantosRicardo da Silva Santos](https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Ricardo-Da-Silva-Santos-2)
- [Murilo Gleyson Gazzola](https://www.researchgate.net/scientific-contributions/Murilo-Gleyson-Gazzola-2339103824)
- [Paulo Marcelino Figueira](https://www.researchgate.net/scientific-contributions/Paulo-Marcelino-Figueira-2339121359)
- [Cristiano Torezzan](https://www.researchgate.net/scientific-contributions/Cristiano-Torezzan-2223878276)

Background Despite rapid advances in large language models (LLMs), automated ICD-10 coding of real-world clinical narratives remains unreliable. A key challenge lies not only in model limitations, but in the intrinsic ambiguity of clinical documentation and the substantial variability among human coders. Methods We benchmarked six general-purpose LLMs for hierarchical ICD-10 coding of 1,117 obstetric discharge summaries written in Brazilian Portuguese. Model performance was evaluated at both category and leaf levels and contextualized against blinded clinician validation to quantify realistic human agreement. We further assessed whether Portuguese-to-English translation or lightweight supervised fine-tuning improved performance. Results Even the best-performing model (GPT-4o) achieved only modest agreement with the human reference, with micro-F1 scores of 0.36 at the three-character level and 0.15 at the leaf level. Translation into English did not yield consistent gains, and direct fine-tuning on code–description pairs failed to improve accuracy. In clinician validation, human-coded references achieved a precision of 0.77, compared to 0.59 for the strongest model, revealing a substantial gap between automated predictions and clinically accepted codes. Conclusions Our findings indicate that current LLMs remain below human-level reliability for autonomous ICD-10 coding in Portuguese. More importantly, they show that conventional evaluation metrics such as F1-score substantially misrepresent clinical usefulness by conflating model error with human disagreement. The primary bottleneck for automated medical coding is therefore not model capacity, but the imperfect and variable human gold standard itself. LLMs should be positioned as decision-support tools that assist, rather than replace, expert clinical coders.

- [Thales Sales Almeida](https://www.researchgate.net/scientific-contributions/Thales-Sales-Almeida-2234305381)

Large Language Models (LLMs) exhibit significant performance variations depending on the linguistic and cultural context in which they are applied. This disparity signals the necessity of mature evaluation frameworks that can assess their capabilities in specific regional settings. In the case of Portuguese, existing evaluations remain limited, often relying on translated datasets that may not fully capture linguistic nuances or cultural references. Meanwhile, native Portuguese-language datasets predominantly focus on structured national exams or sentiment analysis of social media interactions, leaving gaps in evaluating broader linguistic understanding. To address this limitation, we introduce BRoverbs, a dataset specifically designed to assess LLM performance through Brazilian proverbs. Proverbs serve as a rich linguistic resource, encapsulating cultural wisdom, figurative expressions, and complex syntactic structures that challenge the model comprehension of regional expressions. BRoverbs aims to provide a new evaluation tool for Portuguese-language LLMs, contributing to advancing regionally informed benchmarking. The benchmark is available at https://huggingface.co/datasets/Tropic-AI/BRoverbs.

As the capabilities of language models continue to advance, it is conceivable that “one-size-fits-all” model will remain as the main paradigm. For instance, given the vast number of languages worldwide, many of which are low-resource, the prevalent practice is to pretrain a single model on multiple languages. In this paper, we add to the growing body of evidence that challenges this practice, demonstrating that monolingual pretraining on the target language significantly improves models already extensively trained on diverse corpora. More specifically, we further pretrain GPT-J and LLaMA models on Portuguese texts using 3% or less of their original pretraining budget. Few-shot evaluations on Poeta, a suite of 14 Portuguese datasets, reveal that our models outperform English-centric and multilingual counterparts by a significant margin. Our best model, Sabiá-65B, performs on par with GPT-3.5-turbo. By evaluating on datasets originally conceived in the target language as well as translated ones, we study the impact of language-specific pretraining in terms of 1) capturing linguistic nuances and structures inherent to the target language, and 2) enriching the model’s knowledge about a domain or culture. Our results indicate that most benefits stem from the domain-specific knowledge acquired through monolingual pretraining. Finally, we show that our optimized model for Portuguese demonstrates a reduced performance in English tasks, thereby substantiating the inherent compromise in refining models for specific linguistic domains.
